title: Factorized function signature and execution View codes
hypothesis: Factorizing discrete function signatures from reusable Mirror execution codes supports held-out cross-pairings with lower serialized bytes than per-function codes, and Mirror phase angles save bytes over factorized coefficient codes.
physical_object: one shared interpreter with four frequency-signature basis pairs
mirror_coordinate: one Givens phase angle reused across signatures; signature and execution View are independently addressed
logical_multiplicity: four signatures x sixteen phase Views = 64 logical functions
controls: unfactorized full per-pair two-coefficient function codes
factorized signature ids plus ordinary two-value phase codes
factorized signature ids plus one-angle Mirror phase codes
fixture: f(x;s,phi)=sin(omega_s*x+phi), omega_s={1,2,3,4}; 64 pairings; 16 held-out pairings withheld from the explicit pair table but reconstructed from reusable signatures and phase codes

development.selection_metric: held-out max absolute routing error, NRMSE2, and actual payload bytes

fresh.run_only_if: not applicable; deterministic exhaustive pairing screen

storage.format: torch.save exact inference state including all IDs, codes and metadata

compute.proxy: count shared basis evaluation, code decode and pair lookup; report signature/code table sizes and measured query latency

success_gate: Both seeds: 100% exact held-out routing; held-out NRMSE2 <=1e-6; factorized Mirror payload smaller than both unfactorized table and factorized ordinary coefficient-code bank.
failure_gate: Any routing, held-out quality or actual-byte gate misses.
boundaries: Analytic Fourier family only; no learned Neural Interpreter weights.
No natural task or language generalization claim.
All cross-pair functions are generated from predeclared signature and code sets.
